agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker a basis for choosing a mule rather than a horse or camel. The blank simply asks for an unseen word from verse 29, so getting it right is a matter of luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The earlier cards do not provide a basis for choosing “day” over “Sabbath” or “month.” The baker can only guess the passage's wording rather than reason out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: After card 15 has already covered verse 39, this card restates Absalom's location and David's longing without moving the passage forward. The closing story-isn't-over line is sufficient without the opening recap.
The opening clause places Absalom in Geshur, drawing on verse 38 and also verse 37, but the card cites only verse 39. Its citation therefore does not begin with the first verse it uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

human.problem: The card draws on 2 Samuel 13:14 and 13:22, both from before this passage, as well as 13:23. Its verses field is "2 Samuel 13:22-23": it includes one outside verse (13:22) but leaves out the other (13:14). Other cards that use outside verses (stop 2 card 4 uses 13:3-5, and stop 2 card 11 uses 3:3) cite only in-passage verses in the field and give the outside references inline. Citing 13:14-23 would take in verses the card doesn't use.
human.question: When a story card uses verses from outside the passage and gives their references inline, should its verses field include those outside verses, or only the passage verses the card tells?

human.problem: All five true or false cards have True as the right answer (stop 1 cards 3 and 10, stop 2 cards 3, 9 and 15). A baker who notices this can answer every true or false card without reasoning.
human.question: Should a walkthrough vary which true or false cards are true and which are false, so the answer isn't predictable?

human.problem: Some cards use facts from outside the passage, and they cite them in different ways. Stop 1 card 1 puts 2 Samuel 13:22 in its verses field ('2 Samuel 13:22-23'), which reaches outside the passage and the stop's range (13:23-29). It cites 13:14 only inline. Stop 2 card 4 (13:3-5) and stop 2 card 11 (3:3) cite their outside facts only inline and keep the verses field to passage verses. Read literally, 'from the first verse it uses to the last' would make stop 1 card 1 '2 Samuel 13:14-23' and stop 2 card 4 '2 Samuel 13:3-32'.
human.question: When a story card uses a fact from outside the passage, should its verses field include that verse, or only the passage verses the card tells, with the outside fact cited inline in the text?
